subject: Automation script failing against Building C closet switch (Port 23 connection refused)
symptom_description: My automated configuration backup and VLAN push script failed when targeting the Building C edge switch (10.0.4.15). Script returned: 'ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused on port 23'. I wrote this script back when we racked gear in Hillsboro. Requesting temporary port 23 allow rule on management firewall so I can fix the trunk VLAN.
resolution_notes: Advised requester that corporate security standard strictly prohibits cleartext Telnet (TCP 23) across management segments due to credential sniffing vulnerability (enable password exposure). Assisted requester in modifying the script to establish an encrypted SSH session on TCP 22 with Ed25519 public key authentication. Verified successful connection and VLAN remediation without opening port 23.

subject: Outlook mail synchronization failing over home and mobile Wi-Fi (Server timeout)
symptom_description: Mail syncs fine when plugged into the docking station at the desk, but fails immediately on home Wi-Fi or coffee shop hotspots. Outlook displays alert: 'Receiving reported error (0x8004210A): The operation timed out waiting for a response from the receiving (POP) server.' Outgoing mail is also stuck in Outbox.
resolution_notes: Remote session into user workstation. Audited account settings: inbound was configured for cleartext legacy POP3 (port 110, unencrypted) and outbound was set to SMTP (port 25). Residential and public ISPs routinely drop outbound port 25 to mitigate spam bots, and port 110 transmits credentials in cleartext. Reconfigured account to modern encrypted standards: Inbound IMAPS on TCP 993 (SSL/TLS implicit), and Outbound authenticated Submission on TCP 587 (STARTTLS). Sent test message; confirmed bidirectional mail flow.

subject: Requesting inbound FTP (Port 21) access to drop Building A HVAC controller firmware backup
symptom_description: Need to upload controller configuration snapshots and telemetry logs from our diagnostic field laptop to the internal facilities repository (192.168.10.85). Vendor installation manual specifies FTP on port 21. Connection attempts fail with connection timeout.
resolution_notes: Declined request to permit unencrypted FTP (TCP 21 / 20) through perimeter firewall, as FTP transmits passwords and configuration files in cleartext. Clarified technical difference between SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol, port 22) and FTPS (FTP over TLS, implicit port 990/989). Vendor appliance supports FTPS. Configured TLS listener on jump host and validated secure encrypted file upload.

subject: Requesting public firewall rule for RDP (Port 3389) from hotel in Seattle
symptom_description: Currently traveling in Seattle for the quarterly close. Need direct Remote Desktop access to my primary finance workstation (192.168.10.14). Please open TCP 3389 on the external IP for the next 72 hours so I can finish the audit deliverables from my hotel room.
resolution_notes: Explained security policy prohibiting raw RDP (TCP 3389) exposure to the public internet due to constant brute-force automated scanning and ransomware threat actor targeting. Provisioned contractor onto corporate VPN client pool with MFA verification. Provided destination address of dedicated jump host accessible only within VPN tunnel. Verified secure session establishment.

subject: Onboarding password reset utility failing from Guest Wi-Fi; Kerberos ticket rejection
symptom_description: Sitting in the 1st floor lobby awaiting permanent desk assignment. Connected to Guest Wi-Fi. Self-service password registration utility fails with 'Cannot contact directory server (LDAP error 81)'. After reconnecting to corporate dock, domain logon reports 'Kerberos pre-authentication failed: Clock skew too great'.
resolution_notes: Diagnosed two underlying issues: 1) Password reset tool was attempting cleartext LDAP (TCP 389) across untrusted guest wireless. Reconfigured client endpoint to use secure LDAPS on TCP 636 with corporate root CA. 2) Client system clock had drifted 14 minutes behind domain controllers, violating Kerberos 5-minute maximum skew tolerance. Triggered resync via NTP (UDP 123) against internal time server (w32tm /resync). Kerberos ticket granting succeeded immediately.

subject: Network monitoring collector polling switches with community string 'public'
symptom_description: Internal audit flagged that newly deployed access switches in Building B are answering SNMP GET requests on UDP 161 using default community string 'public'. Need review of monitoring template before weekly change window.
resolution_notes: SNMP v1 and v2c send community strings across the wire in cleartext plaintext. Migrated network polling configuration to SNMPv3 utilizing SHA-256 for authentication (auth) and AES-128 for payload privacy/encryption (priv). Disabled legacy community string 'public' across all managed interfaces.

subject: Request to permit UDP 514 syslog traffic from guest wireless subnet to central SIEM collector
symptom_description: Working on staging laptops from the guest conference area. Wanted to forward debugging logs to the collector at 192.168.10.60 on UDP 514 without walking back upstairs to plug into the bench rack.
resolution_notes: Denied request to route cleartext UDP 514 across guest boundary. Directed technician to forward log events via Syslog-over-TLS (TCP 6514) with mutual certificate verification, ensuring tamper-proof confidentiality for diagnostic output.

subject: High-volume badge printer in Lobby unresponsive; requires emergency TFTP firmware flash
symptom_description: The badge and visitor pass printer in Main Reception froze during an interrupted auto-update. Recovery mode requires sending binary ROM over TFTP (UDP 69). Requested opening UDP 69 from technician laptop on standard user VLAN.
resolution_notes: TFTP lacks any authentication or encryption mechanisms and is vulnerable to directory traversal and packet spoofing. Refused to broadcast TFTP across corporate workstation VLAN. Moved technician laptop and printer to isolated staging switch on air-gapped maintenance VLAN. Completed firmware upload on UDP 69; closed port immediately.

subject: Plant operations water pump and valve controller telemetry stream connection timeout
symptom_description: Telemetry telemetry gateway in Building 4 (East Treatment Line) failed to stream sensor metrics to central plant ops console. Field technician attempted to route unencrypted Modbus/TCP (port 502) and cleartext DNP3 (port 20000) over the inter-site WAN link. Traffic is currently blocked by edge boundary ACLs. Plant ops requires continuous pressure and flow monitoring to prevent overflow alarms.
resolution_notes: Triage with Leah Moreno (Portland plant operations lead): Industrial control protocols (Modbus 502, DNP3 20000) have zero native encryption or authentication. Permitting raw cleartext telemetry over WAN exposes critical plant actuators to unauthorized command injection. Coordinating with Tier 2 Network Security to encapsulate telemetry into an IPsec ESP tunnel terminated at the plant SCADA boundary firewall. Work in progress.

subject: Shipping dock thermal barcode printers unresponsive; Print Spooler service stopped
symptom_description: All shipping label printers across loading bays 1 through 4 went offline simultaneously at 14:30. Shipping staff cannot generate packing slips or bill of lading manifests. Windows error on print server: 'The Print Spooler service terminated unexpectedly. Error code 0x800706BA (The RPC server is unavailable)'.
resolution_notes: Remoted into print server (PORT-PRN-01). Identified corrupt print job in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS causing spoolsv.exe crash upon RPC (TCP 135) binding. Stopped Print Spooler, purged corrupted .SHD and .SPL files, restarted service, and verified TCP 445 (SMB) and 135 (RPC) listeners active. Successfully released shipping queue.

subject: Executive laptop locked at startup: 'Enter the recovery key for this drive'
symptom_description: Turned on Dell Latitude laptop after rebooting for an automated Dell Command Update / BIOS firmware flash. Screen is bright blue demanding a 48-digit BitLocker recovery key. Executive has a board presentation in 30 minutes.
resolution_notes: Conducted mandatory out-of-band identity verification via voice callback to department manager. Accessed Microsoft Entra / Active Directory administrative portal. Located computer object PORT-NB-0482. Retrieved 48-digit BitLocker recovery key matching Key ID 7B4F-29E1. Read key to user; drive unlocked successfully. Instructed user to suspend BitLocker prior to executing subsequent UEFI/TPM firmware updates.

subject: Active Directory account locking out repeatedly every 5 minutes
symptom_description: Password was changed yesterday morning. Today, account is locking out continuously every 5 to 10 minutes, even when not touching the workstation keyboard. Self-service unlock succeeds and then locks out again.
resolution_notes: Inspected Domain Controller Security log for Event ID 4740 (Account Lockout). Filtered by user 'dkim'. Event 4740 identified Caller Computer Name as 'IPAD-DKIM-04'. Contacted user; discovered personal iPad connected to guest Wi-Fi was still attempting Exchange ActiveSync authentication with expired password, rapidly hitting the 5-attempt bad password threshold. Updated password in iPad Settings; lockout cleared.

subject: Unrecognized high-signal Wi-Fi network 'Portland_Guest_Fast' broadcasting near Conference Room B
symptom_description: Visitors reported seeing a strong unencrypted SSID named 'Portland_Guest_Fast' in the lobby. IT wireless map does not show any access points registered with this SSID in the reception area. Physical inspection revealed a small black travel router plugged into a conference room RJ-45 wall jack.
resolution_notes: Confirmed active rogue access point bridging external wireless devices directly into corporate internal VLAN 10. Immediately unplugged hardware device and confiscated for analysis. Disabled switch port (Fa0/18) on Closet 1A switch. Escalated incident to SOC and physical security for vendor/contractor audit.

subject: Suspicious urgent vendor invoice email with disc image attachment (.iso)
symptom_description: Received email claiming our enterprise enterprise account is 90 days overdue. Sender name says 'Supplier Billing', but email address is 'billing@vendor-invoicing.net'. Email contains attachment named 'INV_Oct2026_9942.pdf.iso'. User has not opened the attachment.
resolution_notes: Extracted raw message headers. Inspected SPF, DKIM, DMARC: SPF failed (origin IP from overseas VPS), DKIM invalid, DMARC policy=none. Attachment extension uses double camouflage (.pdf.iso) to bypass standard document filters and mount a malicious executable payload upon click. Isolated workstation, purged message across mailboxes, and forwarded sample to SOC incident response.
